174	#      itself without root. Enabled when `gui_apps_linux_no_root=true`.
175	#
176	# Docs: see docs/tools/appimage.md for install paths, ail-cli usage, and
177	# the libfuse2 / AppArmor gotchas on recent Ubuntu.
178	# =============================================================================
179	
180	- name: Check if AppImageLauncher is installed (system-wide)
181	  when:
182	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
183	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
184	  ansible.builtin.command: dpkg -s appimagelauncher
185	  register: ail_check
186	  changed_when: false
187	  failed_when: false
188	
189	- name: Install AppImageLauncher via PPA
190	  when:
191	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
192	    - target_architecture != 'armv7l'
193	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
194	    - ail_check.rc != 0
195	  become: true
196	  tags: [sudo]
197	  block:
198	    - name: Add AppImageLauncher PPA
199	      ansible.builtin.apt_repository:
200	        repo: ppa:appimagelauncher-team/stable
201	        state: present
202	        update_cache: true
203	        filename: appimagelauncher-team-stable
204	      ignore_errors: true
205	      register: ail_ppa
206	
207	    - name: Install appimagelauncher from PPA
208	      ansible.builtin.apt:
209	        name: appimagelauncher
210	        state: present
211	      when: ail_ppa is succeeded
212	      register: ail_apt_install
213	      ignore_errors: true
214	  rescue:
215	    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher PPA install failed
216	      ansible.builtin.debug:
217	        msg: "AppImageLauncher PPA install failed — trying GitHub .deb fallback next."
218	
219	- name: Install AppImageLauncher from GitHub .deb (fallback)
220	  when:
221	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
222	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
223	    - not (gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool)
224	    - ail_check.rc != 0
225	    - (ail_apt_install is not defined) or (ail_apt_install is not succeeded)
226	  become: true
227	  tags: [sudo]
228	  block:
229	    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release metadata
230	      ansible.builtin.uri:
231	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
232	        return_content: true
233	      register: ail_release
234	
235	    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher .deb asset URL
236	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
237	        ail_deb_url: >-
238	          {{ (ail_release.json.assets
239	              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher_.*_' + ail_deb_arch + '\\.deb$')
240	              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')
241	              | list
242	              | first) | default('') }}
243	      vars:
244	        ail_deb_arch: "{{ {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64'}[target_architecture] }}"
245	
246	    - name: Download AppImageLauncher .deb
247	      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
248	      ansible.builtin.get_url:
249	        url: "{{ ail_deb_url }}"
250	        dest: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
251	        mode: '0644'
252	        timeout: 180
253	
254	    - name: Install AppImageLauncher .deb
255	      when: ail_deb_url | length > 0
256	      ansible.builtin.apt:
257	        deb: /tmp/appimagelauncher.deb
258	        state: present
259	  rescue:
260	    - name: Warn AppImageLauncher .deb install failed
261	      ansible.builtin.debug:
262	        msg: "AppImageLauncher .deb install failed — the Lite user-level variant is still available via noRoot mode."
263	
264	- name: Install AppImageLauncher Lite (user-level, noRoot)
265	  when:
266	    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'Debian'
267	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'aarch64']
268	    - gui_apps_linux_no_root | bool
269	  block:

271	      ansible.builtin.file:
272	        path: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications"
273	        state: directory
274	        mode: '0755'
275	
276	    - name: Get latest AppImageLauncher release (for Lite variant)
277	      ansible.builtin.uri:
278	        url: https://api.github.com/repos/TheAssassin/AppImageLauncher/releases/latest
279	        return_content: true
280	      register: ail_lite_release
281	
282	    - name: Resolve AppImageLauncher Lite AppImage URL
283	      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
284	        ail_lite_url: >-
285	          {{ (ail_lite_release.json.assets
286	              | selectattr('name', 'match', '^appimagelauncher-lite-.*-' + target_architecture + '\\.AppImage$')
287	              | map(attribute='browser_download_url')

291	    - name: Download AppImageLauncher Lite

295	        dest: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/Applications/appimagelauncher-lite.AppImage"

2	# Infrastructure-as-Code tools role
3	# Tools: Azure CLI (az), Terraform (terraform), OpenTofu (tofu)
4	
5	# =============================================================================
6	# macOS - all via Homebrew
7	# =============================================================================
8	
9	# Each brew install is wrapped in block + rescue with retries because
10	# ghcr.io (Homebrew's bottle CDN) can be slow/unstable on some networks
11	# (especially behind GFW), and `community.general.homebrew` has no built-in
12	# retry. Without retries, a single `curl: (18) Transferred a partial file`
13	# would fail the whole task. Tools also install independently so one failure
14	# doesn't block the others. For GFW users: set `HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN` to a
15	# mirror (see docs/tools/infrastructure-as-code.md).
16	
17	- name: Install Azure CLI (macOS)
18	  when:
19	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Darwin"
20	    - iac_install_azure_cli
21	  block:
22	    - name: Install azure-cli via Homebrew

22	- name: Set mise binary path (user install)
23	  when:
24	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
25	    - mise_user_bin.stat.exists | default(false)
26	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
27	    mise_bin: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin/mise"
28	
29	- name: Set mise binary path (system install)
30	  when:
31	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
32	    - mise_bin is not defined
33	  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
34	    mise_bin: /usr/bin/mise
35	
36	# Install mise tools from ~/.config/mise/config.toml (node@lts)
37	# Non-fatal: mise downloads are flaky and some tools (e.g. ruby) may fail on
38	# constrained hardware. Partial success is fine — user can re-run `mise install`.
39	#
40	# On armv7l (RPi 4 with 32-bit armhf userland), skip bun (no armv7l build),
41	# ruby (ruby-build source compile is too heavy and fragile), and pin node to
42	# @20 — the last LTS with armv7l prebuilts. Node 21+ has no armv7l prebuilt and
43	# source-builds fail linking (`__atomic_load_8`) without `-latomic`.
44	- name: Install mise global tools (Debian/Ubuntu, armv7l)
45	  when:
46	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
47	    - target_architecture in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
48	  ansible.builtin.command:
49	    cmd: "{{ mise_bin }} install --yes node@20 rust@latest"
50	  register: mise_install
51	  changed_when: "'install' in mise_install.stderr or 'install' in mise_install.stdout"
52	  failed_when: false
53	
54	- name: Install mise global tools (Debian/Ubuntu)
55	  when:
56	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
57	    - target_architecture not in ['armv7l', 'armv6l']
58	  ansible.builtin.command:
59	    cmd: "{{ mise_bin }} install --yes"
60	  register: mise_install
61	  changed_when: "'install' in mise_install.stderr or 'install' in mise_install.stdout"
62	  failed_when: false
63	
64	- name: Warn if mise install had failures
65	  when:
66	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
67	    - mise_install.rc is defined
68	    - mise_install.rc != 0
69	  ansible.builtin.debug:
70	    msg: |
71	      mise install exited with rc={{ mise_install.rc }} — some tools may have failed.
72	      Re-run manually to retry: `{{ mise_bin }} install --yes`
73	      Stderr tail: {{ mise_install.stderr_lines[-5:] | default([]) | join(' | ') }}
74	
75	# fzf - upstream clone is managed by .chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl (Linux only,
76	# since the apt version is outdated and lacks --zsh). We only need to build
77	# the binary here; `creates:` makes the task idempotent and lets it re-run
78	# after chezmoi pulls a new release that bumps ~/.fzf/install.
79	- name: Install fzf (binary only, shell integration handled by zsh config)
80	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
81	  ansible.builtin.command:
82	    cmd: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.fzf/install --bin"
83	    creates: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.fzf/bin/fzf"
84	
85	# lazygit
86	- name: Check if lazygit is installed
87	  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
88	  ansible.builtin.command: lazygit --version
89	  register: lazygit_check
90	  changed_when: false
91	  failed_when: false
92	
93	- name: Install lazygit via PPA (Ubuntu only — PPA has no Debian Release file)
94	  when:
95	    - ansible_facts["distribution"] == "Ubuntu"
96	    - lazygit_check.rc != 0
97	  become: true
98	  tags: [sudo]
99	  block:
100	    - name: Add lazygit PPA

## Surface Area Mapping: Adding a New Profile (e.g., `centos_server`)

Based on my inventory of the codebase, here are the **6 surfaces that must stay in lockstep** when adding a new profile like `centos_server`:

### 1. **.chezmoi.toml.tmpl** — Profile prompt block

**File**: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`

**Lines 20-24** (the complete profile prompt block):
```toml
{{- $profileChoices := list "macos" "ubuntu_desktop" "ubuntu_server" }}
{{- $defaultProfile := "ubuntu_server" }}
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }}{{ $defaultProfile = "macos" }}{{ end }}
{{- $profile := promptChoiceOnce . "profile" "Which profile" $profileChoices $defaultProfile }}
profile = {{ $profile | quote }}
```

**How the default is chosen**: OS-aware logic. On macOS (`eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"`), default is `"macos"`. On all other OS (Linux), default is `"ubuntu_server"`. The user is always prompted — there is no silent auto-skip.

**To add `centos_server`**:
- Add to `$profileChoices` list: `list "macos" "ubuntu_desktop" "ubuntu_server" "centos_server"`
- Consider: should it have its own default? If it's Linux-specific and you want to prompt between `ubuntu_server` and `centos_server` on Linux, you'd need to enhance the default logic (currently just macOS vs. everything-else).

**File**: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/Dockerfile`

**Line 8** (the ARG):
```dockerfile

```

**Lines 124-125** (the chezmoi init invocation with the flag):
```dockerfile

    --promptString "profile (ubuntu_server|ubuntu_desktop|macos)=${CHEZMOI_PROFILE}" \
```

**Critical detail**: The flag uses `--promptString` (not `--promptChoice`) and the text must match **exactly** what `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` has as the prompt text (`"Which profile"`). However, the Dockerfile's comment says `"profile (ubuntu_server|ubuntu_desktop|macos)="` — this is **documentation in the comment only** and does NOT match chezmoi's internal matching mechanism.

**To add `centos_server`**:
- Update the comment in line 125 to include `centos_server`: `"profile (ubuntu_server|ubuntu_desktop|macos|centos_server)=${CHEZMOI_PROFILE}"`

**File**: `/Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`

**Lines 632-687** (the `doctor` subcommand and its implementation):

The `doctor` function (lines 654-687) greps three files:

2. `Dockerfile` for `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build arguments (lines 643-648)

It then **cross-checks parity**:

1. **Prompt text match**: The string in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` line 23 (`"Which profile"`) **must exactly match** the `prompt_text` field in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` line 120. This is what `chezmoi init --promptChoice` matches on.

### DETAILED FINDINGS BY ROLE

#### ✅ PORTABLE AS-IS (5 roles)
These roles require **no CentOS-specific branching**:

1. **docker** (line 69: `get.docker.com`)

   - `become: true`, `apt:` module, but the core script is distro-agnostic.  
   - **Status:** Works on CentOS 7 via the convenience script (which installs via yum internally).

2. **dotnet_tools** (user-managed mise; no package manager calls)  
   - Language version manager entirely handles the toolchain.  
   - **Status:** Zero OS coupling.

3. **homebrew** (macOS-only check, no Linux logic)  
   - **Status:** Already Darwin-gated; no change needed.

4. **js_cli_tools** (npm/mise; no apt/yum/snap)  
   - **Status:** Fully portable; just needs Node.js (via mise).

5. **python_uv_tools** (uv tool install; no OS-specific calls)

   - **Fix:** Add RedHat/CentOS block with yum + EPEL for ripgrep/fd (which have better GitHub release fallbacks anyway).

### ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS FOR CENTOS 7.9 SUPPORT

**Package manager:** yum (not dnf—CentOS 7 predates dnf; dnf landed in RHEL 8).

**EOL mirrors:** CentOS 7 reached EOL June 2024. Two options:
- Use `vault.centos.org` mirrors for base + extras + updates.
- Recommend user migrate to CentOS Stream or Rocky Linux 7 (which extends CentOS 7 support).

**EPEL repository:** Many packages live only in EPEL. The bootstrap script should enable `epel-release` before ansible runs.

**Repo differences:**
- **Azure CLI:** Microsoft publishes a RHEL 7 yum repo (`https://aka.ms/azure-cli`).
- **HashiCorp (Terraform/OpenTofu):** Official RHEL yum repo available.
- **Docker:** Convenience script handles yum internally; role just needs to call the script.
- **GitHub releases:** Most roles already have fallbacks to GitHub releases (musl binaries, versioned tarballs). CentOS 7 (glibc 2.17) is below modern glibc requirements; many releases fail. **Mitigations:**
  - Prefer musl-compiled binaries where available (already done in some roles: `fd`, `ripgrep`, `lnav`, etc.).
  - Fall back to source compilation or skip on CentOS 7 for tools without musl releases.

**Linuxbrew (Homebrew on Linux):** Dropped CentOS 7 support in 2024 (glibc 2.17 below minimum). The `homebrew` role on Linux is already a non-starter; roles check for its existence and skip if unavailable (e.g., `llm_tools` line 50-78).

---

### WORK ESTIMATE

**Rough sizing:**

| Task | Effort | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| Add `ansible_os_family == "RedHat"` conditionals to 14 apt roles | 2–4 hours | Mostly copy-paste of apt blocks → yum blocks; straightforward. |
| Create 14 parallel yum task blocks | 3–6 hours | Identify package name mappings (apt → yum); some tools have no yum packages (fallback to GitHub releases). |
| Enable EPEL in bootstrap | 30 min | Single task in pre-playbook. |
| Set up vault.centos.org mirrors for apt_repository/yum_repository | 1–2 hours | Decide on mirror strategy; update 3–4 roles (iac_tools, azure, docker) to use vault mirrors. |
| Test on CentOS 7.9 VM | 2–4 hours | Spin up test box; run `ansible-playbook` with a CentOS 7–specific inventory; debug glibc/binary incompatibilities. |
| Document CentOS 7 limitations (glibc, Linuxbrew, binary availability) | 1 hour | Update CLAUDE.md / docs. |
| **Total** | **9–17 hours** | Conservative estimate; most work is repetitive. |

---

### CRITICAL GLIBC / BINARY CONSIDERATIONS

CentOS 7.9 ships **glibc 2.17**. Many modern GitHub releases target glibc 2.29+. Roles with pre-built binary downloads will fail on CentOS 7 unless they offer musl builds:

**At-risk roles (GitHub releases, no musl fallback or version pin):**
- `devtools` (vhs, freeze, gum, etc.) — need to check upstream release artifacts.
- `networking_tools` (doggo, gping, trippy, bandwhich, rustscan) — already have musl variants or source compilation; mostly OK.
- `neovim` (snap fallback; GitHub releases may not have old glibc variants).
- `bitwarden` (`.deb` is Debian-specific, but npm is portable).

**Mitigation:** For tools without musl releases, fall back to `cargo install` or source build (requires rust + build toolchain, which `lazyvim_deps` + `rust_cargo_tools` already set up).

---

Portable as-is:           7 roles (docker, dotnet_tools, homebrew, js_cli_tools, python_uv_tools, security_tools, starship)
Needs yum branch:        14 roles (base, bitwarden, coding_agents, devtools, gui_apps_linux, iac_tools, input_method, lazyvim_deps, llm_tools, media_tools, neovim, nerdfonts, networking_tools, ruby_gem_tools, zsh)
Desktop-only (skip):      1 role (gui_apps_linux — already implied by Debian-only gating; explicit for CentOS)

Work: ~9–17 hours (mostly repetitive yum block generation + testing)
```

# Add `centos_server` profile (CentOS 7.9)

## Context

User has a CentOS Linux 7.9.2009 box (`yzhang@idc-server104`, internal data
center) and wants to run this dotfiles repo on it the same way `ubuntu_server`
runs on Ubuntu — non-GUI, headless, server-class. Today only three profiles
are recognised: `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`. Falling back to
`ubuntu_server` does not work because every Linux ansible role gates on
`ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` and would be a silent no-op on a
RedHat box; the chezmoi-side configs would deploy but the system tools
(zsh, neovim, ripgrep, etc.) would never get installed.

This plan adds `centos_server` as a sibling of `ubuntu_server` — same tag
set, same `linux.yml` playbook — and ports the foundational ansible roles
to add `ansible_os_family == "RedHat"` branches so a `chezmoi apply` on
CentOS 7.9 actually installs the underlying tools. CentOS 7's age (glibc
2.17, EOL June 2024) means a few roles get **soft-skip** on RedHat rather
than a full port — pragmatic compromise rather than fighting a dead distro.

CLAUDE.md's "no new profile values for OS/arch facts" rule has an explicit
carve-out for user-role choices that can't be auto-detected. CentOS
**isn't** OS/arch (those go through `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch`), but
the **package-manager family** is the load-bearing distinction here.
Chezmoi exposes `.chezmoi.osRelease.id` natively, so we *could* split
`ubuntu_server` into auto-detected behaviour. We deliberately don't:
profile names are already a known UX, the ansible router script already
branches on profile, and "centos_server" makes the divergent role
behaviour discoverable in one place. The fact that `ansible_os_family`
*also* disambiguates inside roles is independent — the chezmoi profile
picks the playbook + tags, ansible facts pick the package manager.

## Open questions for the user

Resolve via AskUserQuestion before final plan:

1. **Scope of ansible role porting** — port all 7 `ubuntu_server`-tagged
   roles to RedHat now, or wire the profile + port only the foundational
   roles (`base`, `zsh`) and soft-skip the rest as TODO?
2. **sudo on idc-server104** — does `yzhang` have passwordless sudo, sudo
   with password, or no sudo? Affects whether to use `noRoot` mode.
3. **EOL repo strategy** — point yum at `vault.centos.org` (frozen
   snapshot from June 2024), or expect the user to handle repo
   configuration outside chezmoi?
4. **Path forward** — is this box being migrated to Rocky/Alma 8 or 9
   soon? If yes, much of this work is throwaway and we should keep it
   minimal.

## Files to modify

### A. Profile wiring (4 files — required regardless of role-port scope)

| # | File | Change |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` line 20 | Add `"centos_server"` to `$profileChoices` list |
| 2 | `Dockerfile` line 125 (comment only) | Update human-readable list `(ubuntu_server\|ubuntu_desktop\|macos\|centos_server)` |
| 3 | `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` line 121 | Add `"centos_server"` to `choices=()` tuple of the `profile` `Prompt(...)` |
| 4 | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` after line 133 | Add `{{ else if eq .profile "centos_server" -}}` branch — same `PLAYBOOK="$ANSIBLE_DIR/playbooks/linux.yml"`, same TAGS as `ubuntu_server` |

After these 4 edits, run `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py
doctor` to verify drift between the three sources.

### B. Ansible role yum branches (foundational subset — recommended scope)

Add `RedHat` blocks to the apt-only roles in `ubuntu_server`'s tag set.
Pattern: copy the existing Debian block, change `os_family` to `"RedHat"`,
swap `ansible.builtin.apt:` → `ansible.builtin.yum:`, swap package names,
keep `become: true` + `tags: [sudo]` so `noRoot` mode skips them
identically to the Debian path.

| Role | Apt packages | RedHat (yum) equivalents | Notes |
|------|--------------|--------------------------|-------|
| `base` | git, git-lfs, curl, wget, ripgrep, fd-find, jq, tree, build-essential | git, git-lfs, curl, wget, jq, tree, gcc, gcc-c++, make, kernel-devel + EPEL: ripgrep, fd-find | EPEL needed; ripgrep/fd already have GitHub-release fallback below the apt block, can broaden the gating to also fire when yum doesn't have the package |
| `zsh` | zsh | zsh | trivial |
| `ruby_gem_tools` | libffi-dev, libyaml-dev | libffi-devel, libyaml-devel | trivial |
| `lazyvim_deps` | lazygit (PPA) + mise-managed tools | lazygit (GitHub release fallback already exists) | broaden distribution check; PPA path doesn't apply, fallback path does |
| `neovim` | neovim (apt → snap → release) | neovim (EPEL) → release fallback | snap path is Debian-only, skip on RedHat |
| `starship` | installer.sh (already portable) | installer.sh | just broaden `os_family` gate to include RedHat |
| `devtools` | ~30 apt packages | varies; see below | LARGE — see strategy below |

**`devtools` strategy** — instead of porting every apt block, add a
single yum bootstrap block at the top that installs the readily-available
RedHat-equivalent packages (`gcc`, `make`, `cmake`, `pkgconfig`, `which`,
`unzip`, `gettext`, `bat`, `htop`, `btop`, `tmux`, `pandoc`,
`fontconfig`, `figlet`, `direnv`, `zoxide` — most via EPEL). The vast
majority of devtools (eza, gh, glow, gum, vhs, freeze, thefuck, yazi,
superfile, sesh, zellij, duckdb, rclone, taplo, television, tailspin,
lnav, dasel, yq, jnv, witr, fastfetch, etc.) already fall back to
GitHub releases or `cargo install` and will work on CentOS 7 if their
binary is glibc-2.17-compatible.

**Mark up-front as out-of-scope on RedHat (soft-skip via `when:
ansible_os_family != "RedHat"`):**

- `gui_apps_linux` — already excluded by `centos_server` tag set; no
  change needed.
- `bitwarden` (the snap/.deb path) — npm fallback already works.
- The few devtools sub-blocks that pull from Ubuntu PPAs (lazygit PPA,
  diffnav apt tap) — fallback paths cover RedHat.

### C. Glibc 2.17 fallout

Several tools install pre-built binaries from GitHub releases that target
glibc 2.29+ (Ubuntu 22.04 era). On CentOS 7 these crash with
`GLIBC_2.29 not found`. **Don't try to fix in this plan** — let them fail
on first run, capture the symptom in `pitfalls/centos7-glibc-217.md` per
the project-knowledge-harness pattern, document the cargo/musl fallback
for each affected tool. Adding a comprehensive musl fallback would
balloon scope.

### D. Documentation

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `README.md` (Quick Setup section, ~line 357) | Add `centos_server` to the `just docker-*` profile examples if a `docker-centos` build target is added (optional — see below) |
| `docs/this_repo/architecture.md` lines 129-136 | Add `centos_server` row to the profile table: OS=CentOS 7+, tags=same as `ubuntu_server` (no nerdfonts, no gui_apps). Add a one-paragraph note about glibc 2.17 / EOL caveats and link to the new pitfalls file |
| `docs/linux-package-sources.md` | Add a section / table row for CentOS+yum if it has the apt/snap/Homebrew matrix (verify during implementation) |
| `pitfalls/centos7-glibc-217.md` (new) | Document the glibc-2.29-not-found symptom, list affected tools, give cargo/musl workarounds |
| `TODO.md` | One `P3 [M]` entry: "Comprehensive devtools yum port + EPEL repo bootstrap for centos_server" if the recommended scope is adopted (foundational-only port) |

### E. NOT in scope (deliberately)

- New `docker-centos` justfile target / Dockerfile — not requested, the
  user wants real-machine support, not a Docker build target. Skip
  unless asked.
- `useChineseMirror` interaction — `idc-server104` hostname suggests
  a Chinese data centre; if `useChineseMirror=true`, the EPEL/yum
  bootstrap would need to point at `mirrors.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn` or
  similar. Mention as a follow-up TODO; don't block this PR on it.
- BUNDLES preset for CentOS — the existing `server-linux` bundle is
  fine; profile is independent of bundle in `dotfiles_init.py`.

## Verification

After implementation:

1. `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor` — exit 0
   (no drift between `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, `Dockerfile`, and `PROMPTS`).
2. `uv run mkdocs build --strict` — no broken links from the new

3. On the CentOS 7.9 box itself, end-to-end:

   - `chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)"` succeeds; new login session loads

4. On the existing macOS / Ubuntu boxes, regression-check by re-running

**How much ansible role porting do you want in this change?**

Options:
- **Foundational only (Recommended)** - Wire the centos_server profile + add RedHat (yum) branches to base, zsh, ruby_gem_tools, lazyvim_deps, neovim, starship. Soft-skip devtools' apt-only packages (most have GitHub/cargo fallbacks that work). Lands a usable shell + editor; documents the rest as a P3 TODO.
- **Full ubuntu_server tag set** - Port all 7 roles in ubuntu_server's tag set, including a comprehensive yum block in devtools. Bigger PR, more testing needed on the actual CentOS box, but everything that works on Ubuntu server should work on CentOS.
- **Profile wiring only** - Just add the centos_server choice to the 4 lockstep files and route to linux.yml. Don't touch any ansible roles — you'll yum-install zsh/git/etc. by hand, chezmoi just deploys configs. Useful if the box already has tools installed or you'll migrate to Rocky soon.

**What's the sudo situation on idc-server104?**

Options:
- **Passwordless sudo** - yzhang has NOPASSWD sudo. Standard run_*.sh.tmpl flow works as-is; no special handling.
- **Sudo with password** - Standard sudo. The shared-sudo-session helper (scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) prompts once at the start of chezmoi apply; downstream scripts reuse the cache.
- **No sudo at all** - Use noRoot mode (--skip-tags sudo). Foundational role port becomes much smaller — only user-level installs (cargo, mise, GitHub releases). yum-installs would be skipped entirely.

**Is this CentOS 7.9 box being migrated to Rocky/Alma 8/9 or CentOS Stream soon?**

Options:
- **No, staying on CentOS 7** - Treat CentOS 7.9 as a long-lived target. Plan the work, eat the glibc-2.17 / EOL-mirror complexity, document the pitfalls thoroughly.
- **Yes, migrating soon** - Migration is in flight (months, not quarters). Keep this minimal — wire the profile + bare-minimum role ports — and revisit after migration. Most of the glibc-2.17 / EOL-vault repo work would be throwaway.
- **Unknown / not my decision** - Treat as CentOS 7 for now but design conservatively — anything that's CentOS-7-specific gets a clear comment so it can be ripped out cleanly if the box gets rebuilt as Rocky 8/9 later.

# Add `centos_server` profile (CentOS 7.9, no sudo)

## Context

User has a corporate CentOS Linux 7.9.2009 box (`yzhang@idc-server104`)
where `sudo -v` fails with PAM permission denied — i.e. no sudo at all.
Wants to run this dotfiles repo on it the same shape as `ubuntu_server`:
no GUI, headless, server-class. Today only three profiles are recognised
(`macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`); falling back to
`ubuntu_server` does not work because every Linux ansible role gates on
`ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` — including the **user-level
GitHub-release fallback blocks** that don't need sudo. So on a CentOS
box even the no-sudo install paths get skipped, and `chezmoi apply`
deploys configs that point at binaries that were never installed.

The big realization from the scope conversation: **on a noRoot CentOS
box, the load-bearing fix isn't adding yum branches — it's broadening
the `os_family == "Debian"` gates on the user-level fallback paths so
they fire on RedHat too.** The apt blocks are tagged `[sudo]` and
already skipped by `--skip-tags sudo` under noRoot mode; the GitHub
release / cargo / mise paths are user-level and don't need sudo, but
they're currently dead-coded for RedHat by an `os_family` predicate
that has no business being on the user-level path.

The migration target is unknown (the box may stay on CentOS 7 long-term
or get rebuilt as Rocky 8/9). Plan accordingly: any CentOS-7-specific
workaround (glibc 2.17 musl preference, EPEL repo bootstrap) gets a
clear comment so it can be ripped out cleanly if the box gets rebuilt.

## Confirmed scope (from clarifying questions)

- **Role port:** Foundational-only. Wire profile + targeted role tweaks.
  Don't comprehensively port `devtools` to yum.
- **Sudo:** None. `noRoot=true` is mandatory at the prompt; user must
  pass `noRoot=true` (or accept the default if the prompt has the right
  default for CentOS, which today it doesn't — see TODO at end).
- **Migration:** Unknown. Add CentOS-7-specific bits with comments so
  they're cheap to remove later.

## Files to modify

### A. Profile wiring — 4 lockstep files (REQUIRED)

| # | File | Edit |
|---|------|------|
| 1 | `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` line 20 | Append `"centos_server"` to `$profileChoices`: `list "macos" "ubuntu_desktop" "ubuntu_server" "centos_server"` |
| 2 | `Dockerfile` line 125 (comment only) | Update comment to `(ubuntu_server\|ubuntu_desktop\|macos\|centos_server)`. ARG on line 8 stays as-is (just a default value). |
| 3 | `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` line 121 | Append `"centos_server"` to `choices=()` of the `Prompt("profile", …)` |
| 4 | `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` after line 133 | Add `{{ else if eq .profile "centos_server" -}}` branch. `PLAYBOOK="$ANSIBLE_DIR/playbooks/linux.yml"` (same as `ubuntu_server`). `TAGS="base,zsh,starship,neovim,lazyvim_deps,devtools,docker,security_tools,rust_cargo_tools,ruby_gem_tools"` (same as `ubuntu_server`). Comment line above it: "CentOS Server: same as Ubuntu Server; user-level fallbacks only on noRoot, see pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md" |

After these 4 edits:
- `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor` must exit 0.
- `chezmoi execute-template < .chezmoi.toml.tmpl` (with profile=centos_server)
  must round-trip cleanly.

### B. Ansible: broaden Debian-only gates on user-level fallback paths

Pattern in `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml` (and applies similarly
elsewhere) — there are 16 hits of `os_family == "Debian"` in that role
alone. Two distinct kinds:

**Kind 1: sudo-tagged apt block** (lines ~19, 38, 219-220, 257-268, 340-349, 359-368, 384-385):
\```yaml
- name: Install base packages (Debian/Ubuntu)
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
  become: true
  tags: [sudo]
  ansible.builtin.apt: ...
\```
Leave alone OR add a parallel `RedHat` branch with `yum:` (tags: [sudo],
become: true) — won't fire on noRoot but useful future-proofing for any
other CentOS user with sudo. **Recommend: add parallel RedHat blocks
only for the trivial cases** (zsh, ruby_gem_tools libffi-devel /
libyaml-devel) and leave large ones (devtools, gui_apps_linux) alone.

**Kind 2: user-level fallback gate** (lines 49-50, 56-58, 132-133, 139-141, 219-220 → wait that's kind 1 — re-examine; the GitHub release blocks are at 56-129, 139-211, 258-281, 348-378, etc.):
\```yaml
- name: Re-check if ripgrep is installed
  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"   # <-- BUG for CentOS
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v rg
  ...

- name: Install ripgrep from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"     # <-- BUG for CentOS
    - rg_recheck.rc != 0
  block: ...
\```
**Fix: broaden these to** `ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`.
For CentOS 7 specifically, the existing musl preference for ripgrep / fd
already does the right thing (musl tarballs ignore glibc version, so
glibc 2.17 is fine).

Concrete files + line ranges to broaden (from the grep run during
exploration):

| Role | File | Lines to broaden |
|------|------|------------------|
| `base` | `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml` | 50, 58, 133, 141, 220, 228, 258, 268, 281, 341, 349, 360, 368, 385 — for each, identify whether it's a "command -v X recheck" or a GitHub-release `block:` (those are the user-level paths that need broadening). Do NOT broaden the apt-tasks (lines 20, 39, 219). |
| `zsh` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh/tasks/main.yml` | Line 13 is the apt block — leave. The user-level `chsh` path (lines 41-66) already gates on `os_family != "Darwin"`, so it works on RedHat as-is. **Required precondition for noRoot CentOS: zsh must already be on `$PATH`** (corporate CentOS boxes typically ship zsh). Captured in pitfalls below. |
| `lazyvim_deps`, `neovim`, `starship`, `security_tools`, `rust_cargo_tools` | spot-check during implementation | Apply the same broadening rule: any user-level / non-sudo path gated on `Debian` should become `in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`. Stop at the first role where the audit becomes painful — note as TODO. |

**Implementation procedure:** open each file, walk top-to-bottom, for
each `os_family == "Debian"` predicate ask "is this on a sudo-tagged
task?" If yes, leave alone (or add parallel RedHat block for the
trivial ones). If no, broaden to `in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`.

### C. Add minimal yum branches (future-proofing only)

Trivial cases where adding a yum block is one-screen of yaml and unlocks
sudo-able CentOS boxes for future users / a future yzhang with sudo:

- `base` role: parallel `Install base packages (RedHat)` block —
  `yum:` install of `git, git-lfs, curl, wget, jq, tree, gcc, gcc-c++,
  make`. Skip ripgrep/fd from yum (they're EPEL-only on CentOS 7 and
  the GitHub-release path is more reliable). `become: true`, `tags:
  [sudo]`.
- `zsh` role: parallel `Install zsh (RedHat)` block. Trivial.
- `ruby_gem_tools` role: parallel block for `libffi-devel,
  libyaml-devel`. Trivial.

Skip yum porting for: `devtools` (huge), `neovim` (EPEL situation
fragile), `lazyvim_deps` (lazygit not in standard RedHat repos),
`security_tools` (already cross-distro). Document the skip in a TODO
entry per project-knowledge-harness pattern.

### D. Pitfalls + documentation

**New file: `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`** — cover symptom-first per
the project-knowledge-harness rule:

- **Symptom:** `chezmoi apply` on CentOS 7 with noRoot=true completes
  cleanly but `command -v rg` / `fd` / `nvim` returns nothing — the
  binaries were never installed.
- **Root cause:** Debian-only `when:` predicates on user-level
  fallback paths.
- **Fix:** broadening pattern (cite this commit).
- **CentOS-7-specific notes:** glibc 2.17 means prefer musl assets;
  upstream `fd` and `ripgrep` already ship musl. Tools that DO ship
  glibc-only binaries (some Go releases, some Rust releases without

- **Required preconditions on a noRoot CentOS box:** `zsh` and `git`
  must already be system-installed (verified `which zsh git`); the
  ansible role can't install them without sudo.
- **Migration note:** if rebuilt as Rocky 8/9, glibc-2.17 caveats go
  away; the gate-broadening (B) is still correct on Rocky.

**`docs/this_repo/architecture.md` lines 129-136** — add row to the
profile table:
\```markdown
| `centos_server` | CentOS 7+ (RedHat family) | Same as `ubuntu_server`. **noRoot recommended** — see `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`. |
\```
Plus a one-paragraph note on why this is its own profile rather than
auto-detected via `.chezmoi.osRelease.id` (cite CLAUDE.md's "profile is
for user-role choices, but package-manager-family is load-bearing for
ansible role behaviour" carve-out — the chezmoi profile picks the
playbook + tags, ansible facts pick the package manager, separation is
clean).

**`mkdocs.yml`** — add nav entry for the new pitfalls page if pitfalls
are in the nav (verify; if `pitfalls/` is referenced via absolute

**`README.md`** — only update if there's a "Supported Platforms"

**`docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md`** — if it has the predicate

  when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"   # <-- BUG for CentOS
  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v rg
  ...

- name: Install ripgrep from GitHub releases (user-level, no sudo)
  when:
    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"     # <-- BUG for CentOS
    - rg_recheck.rc != 0
  block: ...
```
**Fix: broaden these to** `ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`.
For CentOS 7 specifically, the existing musl preference for ripgrep / fd
already does the right thing (musl tarballs ignore glibc version, so
glibc 2.17 is fine).

Concrete files + line ranges to broaden (from the grep run during
exploration):

| Role | File | Lines to broaden |
|------|------|------------------|
| `base` | `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml` | 50, 58, 133, 141, 220, 228, 258, 268, 281, 341, 349, 360, 368, 385 — for each, identify whether it's a "command -v X recheck" or a GitHub-release `block:` (those are the user-level paths that need broadening). Do NOT broaden the apt-tasks (lines 20, 39, 219). |
| `zsh` | `dot_ansible/roles/zsh/tasks/main.yml` | Line 13 is the apt block — leave. The user-level `chsh` path (lines 41-66) already gates on `os_family != "Darwin"`, so it works on RedHat as-is. **Required precondition for noRoot CentOS: zsh must already be on `$PATH`** (corporate CentOS boxes typically ship zsh). Captured in pitfalls below. |
| `lazyvim_deps`, `neovim`, `starship`, `security_tools`, `rust_cargo_tools` | spot-check during implementation | Apply the same broadening rule: any user-level / non-sudo path gated on `Debian` should become `in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`. Stop at the first role where the audit becomes painful — note as TODO. |

**Implementation procedure:** open each file, walk top-to-bottom, for
each `os_family == "Debian"` predicate ask "is this on a sudo-tagged
task?" If yes, leave alone (or add parallel RedHat block for the
trivial ones). If no, broaden to `in ["Debian", "RedHat"]`.

### C. Add minimal yum branches (future-proofing only)

Trivial cases where adding a yum block is one-screen of yaml and unlocks
sudo-able CentOS boxes for future users / a future yzhang with sudo:

- `base` role: parallel `Install base packages (RedHat)` block —
  `yum:` install of `git, git-lfs, curl, wget, jq, tree, gcc, gcc-c++,
  make`. Skip ripgrep/fd from yum (they're EPEL-only on CentOS 7 and
  the GitHub-release path is more reliable). `become: true`, `tags:
  [sudo]`.
- `zsh` role: parallel `Install zsh (RedHat)` block. Trivial.
- `ruby_gem_tools` role: parallel block for `libffi-devel,
  libyaml-devel`. Trivial.

Skip yum porting for: `devtools` (huge), `neovim` (EPEL situation
fragile), `lazyvim_deps` (lazygit not in standard RedHat repos),
`security_tools` (already cross-distro). Document the skip in a TODO
entry per project-knowledge-harness pattern.

### D. Pitfalls + documentation

**New file: `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`** — cover symptom-first per
the project-knowledge-harness rule:

- **Symptom:** `chezmoi apply` on CentOS 7 with noRoot=true completes
  cleanly but `command -v rg` / `fd` / `nvim` returns nothing — the
  binaries were never installed.
- **Root cause:** Debian-only `when:` predicates on user-level
  fallback paths.
- **Fix:** broadening pattern (cite this commit).
- **CentOS-7-specific notes:** glibc 2.17 means prefer musl assets;
  upstream `fd` and `ripgrep` already ship musl. Tools that DO ship
  glibc-only binaries (some Go releases, some Rust releases without
  musl variants) will fail with `GLIBC_2.X not found` — symptom + the
  cargo-source-build workaround.
- **Required preconditions on a noRoot CentOS box:** `zsh` and `git`
  must already be system-installed (verified `which zsh git`); the
  ansible role can't install them without sudo.
- **Migration note:** if rebuilt as Rocky 8/9, glibc-2.17 caveats go
  away; the gate-broadening (B) is still correct on Rocky.

**`docs/this_repo/architecture.md` lines 129-136** — add row to the
profile table:
```markdown
| `centos_server` | CentOS 7+ (RedHat family) | Same as `ubuntu_server`. **noRoot recommended** — see `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md`. |
```
Plus a one-paragraph note on why this is its own profile rather than
auto-detected via `.chezmoi.osRelease.id` (cite CLAUDE.md's "profile is
for user-role choices, but package-manager-family is load-bearing for
ansible role behaviour" carve-out — the chezmoi profile picks the
playbook + tags, ansible facts pick the package manager, separation is
clean).

**`mkdocs.yml`** — add nav entry for the new pitfalls page if pitfalls
are in the nav (verify; if `pitfalls/` is referenced via absolute
GitHub URL only, no nav change needed).

**`README.md`** — only update if there's a "Supported Platforms"
table; from exploration there isn't one explicitly, so no change
needed unless we want to add CentOS to the prose. Defer.

**`docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md`** — if it has the predicate
table, add a row for "RedHat family detection: `eq
.chezmoi.osRelease.id "centos"` or similar" with a link to the
profile-vs-osRelease decision rationale. Verify file exists during
implementation.

- `gui_apps_linux` — already excluded by `centos_server` tag set; no

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
```

```md
# `centos_server` profile on a noRoot CentOS 7 box installs nothing

## Symptom

Run `chezmoi apply` on a CentOS Linux 7.9 box where the user has no
`sudo` (typical corporate/data-center development server):

\```
$ sudo -v
sudo: PAM account management error: Permission denied
sudo: a password is required
\```

`chezmoi apply` completes cleanly, ansible reports `0 failed`, configs
deploy under `~/.config/`, but `command -v rg fd jq nvim starship`
returns nothing. The dotfiles-deployed `~/.zshrc` references binaries
that don't exist; opening a new shell prints `command not found` for
half the prompt.

## Root cause

The Linux ansible roles have two parallel install paths for each tool:

1. **System-level** (`apt:` / `yum:`) — gated by `become: true, tags:
   [sudo]`. Skipped on `noRoot=true` via `--skip-tags sudo`. Correct.
2. **User-level fallback** — downloads pre-built binaries from GitHub
   releases into `~/.local/bin/`, no sudo required.

The user-level fallback is the one that's *supposed* to fire on a
noRoot box. It was historically gated on
`when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"` — which made sense when
the only Linux profiles were `ubuntu_*`, but is wrong as soon as a
RedHat-family box (CentOS, Rocky, Alma) shows up. The user-level path
has no apt-specific behaviour — it's `curl | tar | install`. There's
no reason for it to be gated on the package-manager family.

So on CentOS 7 with `noRoot=true`, both paths are gated out:

- system-level: skipped by `--skip-tags sudo`
- user-level: skipped by `os_family == "Debian"` predicate

The role is a no-op and the user gets a working `~/.zshrc` pointing at
binaries that were never installed.

## Fix

Broaden the user-level (non-sudo-tagged) `when:` predicates from:

\```yaml
when: ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
\```

to:

\```yaml
when: ansible_facts["os_family"] in ["Debian", "RedHat"]
\```

Applied across `dot_ansible/roles/{base,starship,security_tools,rust_cargo_tools}/tasks/main.yml`
when the `centos_server` profile was introduced. The
`Re-check if X is installed` + `Install X from GitHub releases
(user-level, no sudo)` block pattern is the canonical shape — every
file that has it needs the broadening.

**Don't** broaden the sudo-tagged `apt:` blocks the same way — those
have `become: true, tags: [sudo]` and use `ansible.builtin.apt:` which
fails on RedHat. Either leave them alone (skipped under `--skip-tags
sudo` anyway) or add a parallel `RedHat` block with `ansible.builtin.yum:`.

## CentOS 7-specific notes (glibc 2.17)

CentOS 7 ships glibc 2.17 (released 2012). Many modern GitHub-release
binaries are built on Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 (glibc 2.35+) and crash
with:

\```
./tool: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.29' not found (required by ./tool)
\```

The user-level fallbacks in `base/tasks/main.yml` already prefer
**musl** assets where upstream offers them — `ripgrep`, `fd`, `lnav`
all ship `*-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` variants that are statically
linked and ignore glibc version. Those are fine on CentOS 7.

Tools that ship glibc-only binaries (some Go releases, some Rust
releases without musl variants) will fail. Workarounds, in order of
preference:

1. **Cargo source build** — `cargo install <crate>` works on CentOS 7
   via the user's mise/cargo toolchain (`rust_cargo_tools` role
   already sets this up).
2. **Older release pin** — find a release built before the upstream
   project moved to a newer Ubuntu CI, pin to it.
3. **Skip on CentOS 7** — for tools that aren't critical, gate the
   block on `ansible_distribution_major_version != "7"` and live
   without it.

If the box gets rebuilt as Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 (glibc 2.28 / 2.34), most
of these go away — the gate-broadening fix above is still correct on
those.

## Required preconditions on a noRoot CentOS box

The dotfiles can't install **everything** without sudo. On
`centos_server` + `noRoot=true`, verify before running `chezmoi apply`:

- `command -v zsh` resolves — `zsh` package install needs sudo. Most
  corporate CentOS 7 boxes ship zsh; if not, ask the admin to
  `yum install zsh`.
- `command -v git` resolves — same story.
- `chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)"` — depends on the box's chsh policy
  (usually no sudo needed but `/etc/shells` must list zsh's path).

## Migration note

If/when this CentOS 7 box gets rebuilt as Rocky/Alma 8 or 9 (or any
modern RedHat-family distro), the gate-broadening change in this fix
remains correct (`os_family == "RedHat"` still matches). The
glibc-2.17 caveat goes away. The `yum:` blocks added to `base`,
`zsh`, `ruby_gem_tools` continue to work — `yum:` is an alias for
`dnf:` on RHEL 8+ via the ansible compatibility shim.

## Related

- `dot_ansible/roles/base/tasks/main.yml` — canonical
  `Re-check if X / Install X from GitHub releases (user-level)`
  pattern.
- `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`
  — `centos_server` profile branch + `--skip-tags sudo` on
  `noRoot=true`.
- `pitfalls/ansible-missing-sudo-tag.md` — sibling pitfall: the
  inverse of this one (sudo task without the `[sudo]` tag, fails on
  noRoot).

```

131	| Profile | OS | Tags Included |
132	|---------|-----|---------------|
133	| `macos` | macOS | homebrew, base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, nerdfonts, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools (alacritty via Brewfile cask) |
134	| `ubuntu_desktop` | Ubuntu | base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, nerdfonts, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools, gui_apps |
135	| `ubuntu_server` | Ubuntu | base, zsh, starship, neovim, lazyvim_deps, devtools, docker, security_tools, rust_cargo_tools, ruby_gem_tools |

141	- **macOS only**: homebrew
142	- **Optional** (via chezmoi config): coding_agents, bitwarden, python_uv_tools, js_cli_tools, llm_tools, input_method (desktop only), networking_tools, iac_tools
143	
144	`ubuntu_server` excludes `nerdfonts` (no GUI needed).
145	
146	## No-root mode (Linux)
147	
148	For Linux servers without sudo/root access, enable `noRoot = true` during `chezmoi init`:
149	
150	```bash
151	chezmoi init --force  # Answer "y" to "No sudo/root access" prompt
152	```
153	
154	This skips all tasks tagged with `[sudo]` (apt packages, system-level installations). Tools with user-level fallbacks are automatically installed to `~/.local/bin`.
155	
156	**User-level tools** (installed automatically without sudo):
157	
158	- **GitHub binaries**: neovim, ripgrep, fd, jq, just, bat, bats, eza, delta, yazi, superfile, zellij, btop, gitleaks, lazygit, fzf, sesh, taplo, television
159	- **tmux-appimage** (x86_64 only): extracted AppImage → `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/squashfs-root`, shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`. Runs only when system `tmux` is older than 3.3.
```

profile: add centos_server (RedHat family, noRoot-first)

Wires a new chezmoi profile so a CentOS 7+ / Rocky / Alma box can be set
up with the same playbook + tag set as ubuntu_server. Profile is
deliberately its own surface (not auto-detected via osRelease.id) because
the divergent ansible behaviour is package-manager-family scoped — the
chezmoi profile picks playbook+tags, ansible_os_family picks apt vs yum.

The load-bearing fix on a noRoot CentOS box is broadening the
os_family=="Debian" predicates on user-level GitHub-release / cargo /
mise fallback paths to in ["Debian", "RedHat"]. Without this they no-op
on RedHat even though they don't need sudo. Applied to base, starship,
security_tools (gitleaks), rust_cargo_tools (pueue + systemd user
service). Trivial parallel yum: blocks added to base, zsh,
ruby_gem_tools for future-proofing sudo-able RedHat hosts.

devtools / neovim / lazyvim_deps / docker still gated Debian-only on
user-level paths — captured in TODO.md (P3 [M]) for follow-up. Pitfall
pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md documents the pattern, glibc 2.17 caveats,
and the precondition that zsh/git must be pre-installed on a sudoless
box.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

`grep -A 30 "Workaround\|Fix\|Resolution" /Users/daviddwlee84/.local/share/chezmoi/pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md | head -50`

```text
## Fix (the atomic pipeline)

Do the redaction without ever printing the matched bytes, then stage and
commit in **one** bash command so SpecStory has no window to write a new
copy:

```bash
FILE=.specstory/history/<active-session>.md

# 1. Redact in place. NEVER use grep/awk/sed in a way that prints the match.
python3 -c "
import re, pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('$FILE')
s = p.read_text()
s2 = re.sub(r'ey[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}',
            '<REDACTED-JWT>', s)
p.write_text(s2)
"

# 2. Stage the redacted snapshot. From this moment, the index is frozen —
# any later specstory write only affects the worktree, not the commit.
git add "$FILE"

# 3. Commit. Pre-commit will stash any post-stage worktree drift, run on
# the staged (redacted) version, find nothing, and commit cleanly.
git commit -m "..."
```

The redaction regex above (`ey[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.{10,}\.{10,}`) is
JWT-shaped (3 base64url segments separated by dots) and catches the common
case. Adjust per the actual leak class.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
# ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — fleet_apply.py host inventory
#
# Seeded ONCE by chezmoi (`create_` prefix) so your edits are never overwritten.
# To reset to this template: `rm ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml && chezmoi apply`.
# File mode is 0600 (chezmoi `private_` prefix) — safe for plaintext passwords,
# but Bitwarden / interactive prompt sources are still preferred.
#
# Schema reference: docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md
# Run: `just fleet-apply` (parallel) | `just fleet-apply-dry-run` (chezmoi diff)

[defaults]
chezmoi_path    = "auto"           # "auto" → augment remote PATH with common install dirs
                                   # (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin,
                                   #  /usr/local/bin, /snap/bin) before invoking `chezmoi`.
                                   # Override per-host with an absolute path (e.g.
                                   # "/snap/bin/chezmoi") to pin a specific binary.
connect_timeout = 150
command_timeout = 18000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Examples — DELETE these and add your own [[hosts]] entries.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1) Preferred: ssh_config alias. Inherits ProxyJump, IdentityAgent (e.g.
#    1Password SSH agent), Match blocks — everything you'd get from `ssh lab-box`.
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "lab-box"
# ssh_alias       = "lab-box"
# no_root_machine = false                                   # remote was init'd with noRoot=false
# password_source = { type = "bitwarden", item = "ssh-lab-box-sudo" }

# 2) Explicit connection (no ssh_config entry).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "vps-tokyo"
# hostname        = "203.0.113.42"
# user            = "dwlee"
# port            = 22
# identity_file   = "~/.ssh/id_ed25519"
# no_root_machine = true                                    # remote was init'd with noRoot=true
# # password_source omitted → no sudo phase; chezmoi runs as the SSH user only.

# 3) Interactive prompt (asked once at startup, never persisted).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "office-mac"
# ssh_alias       = "office-mac"
# no_root_machine = false
# password_source = { type = "prompt" }

# 4) Plaintext password (last resort — relies on file mode 0600).
# [[hosts]]
# name            = "throwaway-vm"
# ssh_alias       = "throwaway-vm"
# no_root_machine = false
# password_source = { type = "plain", value = "hunter2" }

# 5) Local execution (this machine, no SSH). Useful when you want
#    `just fleet-apply` to keep the orchestrator itself in sync along
#    with the SSH hosts. ssh_alias / hostname / user / port /
#    identity_file are ignored. Sudo is inherited from the parent
#    terminal (chezmoi may prompt for password if it needs root).
[[hosts]]
name            = "self"
local           = true
no_root_machine = false                                    # set false if your local apply needs sudo

no_root_machine = false
password_source = { type = "plain", value = "Z1112H" }

no_root_machine = false
password_source = { type = "plain", value = "tln-aDmin1" }

[[hosts]]

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 10:53:25Z)**_

## Diagnosis

`fleet_apply.py` failed at the **SSH layer**, not the chezmoi/sudo layer. Root cause:

**The CentOS 7 sshd on `10.10.10.104` accepts only `gssapi-keyex, gssapi-with-mic, keyboard-interactive`** — no `publickey`, no `password`. Verified via `ssh -v zyc_friend`:

```
debug1: Authentications that can continue: gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,keyboard-interactive
yzhang@10.10.10.104: Permission denied
```

`fleet_apply.py` uses `asyncssh.connect()` and relies on **SSH key auth** — its `_connect_kwargs()` only passes `client_keys`, never `password`. Your interactive `ssh zyc_friend` works because OpenSSH client falls back to `keyboard-interactive` and prompts you for the password; `asyncssh` in fleet_apply has no PAM-prompt fallback path.

The plaintext `password_source = { type = "plain", value = "tadronaut" }` in `~/.config/fleet/machines.toml` is wired for **remote sudo**, not for SSH login. Even if SSH succeeded, this CentOS box has no sudo (your earlier PAM denial), so `no_root_machine = true` (which you set correctly) tells fleet_apply to skip pushing it to `~/.cache/chezmoi-fleet/sudo.pass`.

## Three paths forward (pick one)

**1. Bootstrap by hand (fastest — recommended for single host).**

```bash
ssh zyc_friend            # type password interactively
# on the remote:
sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- init --apply daviddwlee84
# answer: profile=centos_server, noRoot=true at the prompts
```

This skips fleet-apply entirely and runs chezmoi directly on the box. Best for single-host setup.

**2. Get the admin to enable pubkey auth.**

Ask the IDC admin to set `PubkeyAuthentication yes` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config` and restart sshd, then `ssh-copy-id zyc_friend`. After that fleet-apply will work. Most useful if you'll re-apply often.

**3. Patch fleet_apply.py to support keyboard-interactive auth.**

Add password-based SSH auth as a new `Host.ssh_password` field (separate from `sudo_password`); pass it to `asyncssh.connect(password=...)`. asyncssh will try password first then keyboard-interactive automatically. ~30-line change in `_connect_kwargs()` + `Host` + machines.toml schema. Worth doing if you'll fleet-manage other CentOS-style hosts later.

For today, **path 1** (bootstrap by hand) is what I'd do — gets you the centos_server profile validated end-to-end with the least yak-shaving. Want me to draft the path-3 patch as a follow-up TODO?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 12:41:34Z)**_

Found the smoking gun. Line 284: `uv tool install ansible-core` runs with no `--python` flag, so uv picks **system Python 3.6.8** on CentOS 7 and resolves `ansible-core` to **2.11.12** (last version supporting Py3.6, released August 2021). That ancient ansible doesn't understand the new Galaxy NG API at `galaxy.ansible.com`, so the collection install crashes with a `KeyError` masquerading as the URL string.

Two compounding issues:
1. **Old Python → old ansible**: 2.11.12 predates Galaxy NG migration
2. **Old ansible → Galaxy NG handshake fails**: `/api/v3/plugin/ansible/content/published/collections/...` is Pulp/Galaxy-NG-shape; 2.11 can't parse the response

Fix: pin uv to Python 3.13 — same pattern already used for `pre-commit` in `security_tools` role. Let me look at the existing pattern and apply.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 12:43:29Z)**_

Committed as `6111034`. Now here's what to run on the CentOS box to recover:

## On `idc-server104`:

```bash
# 1. Nuke the broken ansible 2.11.12 install
uv tool uninstall ansible-core
rm -rf ~/.local/share/uv/tools/ansible-core

# 2. Pull the bootstrap fix
cd ~/.local/share/chezmoi
git pull

# 3. Re-run chezmoi apply — bootstrap will now install ansible on Python 3.13
chezmoi apply
```

Step 1 is needed because uv leaves the old install intact when the new one gets `--force`'d on a different Python; explicit cleanup is faster than letting `--force` figure it out.

## What was actually broken

Two compounding issues, neither related to your VPN/proxy setup:

1. **`uv tool install ansible-core` had no `--python` flag** — defaulted to system Python 3.6.8 → uv picked `ansible-core==2.11.12` (last Py3.6-compatible, Aug 2021)
2. **2.11.12 predates Galaxy NG** — `galaxy.ansible.com` got migrated to Pulp/Galaxy-NG; old ansible can't parse the new `/api/v3/plugin/ansible/content/published/...` endpoint and throws `KeyError(<URL>)`. The bootstrap's "try setting https_proxy" hint is a red herring on CentOS 7.

The fix pins to `--python 3.13` (same pattern as `pre-commit` in `security_tools`). uv auto-fetches a `python-build-standalone` interpreter — statically linked, glibc-2.17 compatible — so the user-level path keeps working without sudo.

## Other things you'll likely hit next on this box

- **`mise install rust@latest`** will source-build rust; on glibc 2.17 this works but is slow. Cargo crates that need newer glibc may fail at link time.
- **Some GitHub-release fallbacks** may still ship glibc-only binaries (already documented in `pitfalls/centos7-noroot.md` → "glibc 2.17"). Workarounds in priority order: musl variant → cargo source build → skip.
- **`zsh` and `git` must already be system-installed** — without sudo, ansible can't install them. `which zsh git` should resolve before you re-run apply; if zsh is missing, you'll need to ask the IDC admin or just live with bash.

If the next bootstrap completes but a specific role still fails, send me the error and I'll patch.
